text:
Recent work supports separating persistent preferences, recent intent, and multiple latent interests. [Hierarchical long and short-term preference modeling (2025)](https://journal.hep.com.cn/fcs/EN/10.1007/s11704-025-41181-y) uses dynamic routing to extract multiple long-term interest vectors, self-attention for recent interactions, and similarity-based matching with time encoding to fuse them. [MIMAR-SRec (AAAI 2026)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/38489) models intentions across contextual windows, combining intent prototypes, contrastive learning, and robustness to interaction and temporal noise.

The closest match to candidate-conditioned scoring is [D2MFRec (published December 2025)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-31190-z): soft clustering extracts K interest vectors; target-item embeddings determine attention weights over those vectors. A separate Transformer/recent-history branch captures global and short-term preferences, with learned gating and denoising contrastive objectives. Candidate-dependent aggregation allows the same history to produce different representations for different candidate items.

Practical inference for this benchmark: retain SASRec’s contextual sequence states, add a small bank of learned interest queries and a recent-window branch, then use each candidate embedding to attend over the resulting interest vectors. Gate this score with the original final-state score; optionally incorporate timestamp gaps into attention or routing. These are proposed adaptations, not demonstrated benchmark gains. Ablate multi-interest pooling, candidate conditioning, and temporal fusion separately using macro validation HR@10. Cache interest vectors and score catalog items in chunks for full-catalog recommendations; single-GPU feasibility and improvements require measurement.
